name: Agree an installment plan that lets a family pay in parts and keeps them out of the defaulter route
priorityReason: Three other use cases already exempt students on a plan. Without this the exemption has nothing to read.

goal.capability: to agree a schedule of parts instead of one lump sum
goal.outcome: the family pays what they can when they can, and is not chased or fined while they keep to it

secondaryActors.involvement: Receives the request and defines the plan once it is approved.
Approves the request. A plan changes when the school gets its money.

additional.description: A guardian requests an installment arrangement from the parent app.
An installment passes its due date unpaid, which ends the plan's protection (BR-8).

preconditions.condition: The guardian is signed in to the parent app, or asks at the office.
An authenticated session exists. Defining requires Accounts; approving requires School Admin.
The student holds no active plan for the same charge (BR-11).

postConditions: An approved plan exists against the student, holding the number of installments, their amounts and their due dates.
The challan the guardian sees reflects the plan rather than the original single amount.
While the plan is met the student is absent from overdue tracking and accrues no late fee, which is the protection the plan exists to give.
A missed installment ends that protection at once and brings the student onto the overdue list.
The installment amounts total exactly the original charge. A plan changes when the school is paid, never how much.
The guardian has been told the decision, and where approved, the schedule they agreed to.
The original invoice is unchanged. A plan schedules a debt; it does not alter it.
The plan is visible to whoever answers the counter, so a family on a plan is not treated as a defaulter by somebody who did not know.

dataFields.name: Invoice
dataFields.validation: The issued invoice the plan schedules.

dataFields.name: Reason for request
dataFields.validation: 20 to 500 characters, written by the guardian. What the School Admin weighs when deciding (BR-2).
dataFields.example: My employer has delayed salaries by two months. I can pay half now and half in October.

dataFields.name: Number of installments
dataFields.validation: 2 or more, and not more than the configured maximum.

dataFields.name: Installment amount
dataFields.validation: Per installment. Together they must total exactly the outstanding charge (BR-4).

dataFields.name: Installment due date
dataFields.validation: Per installment. Each later than the last, and all within the academic session (BR-5).

dataFields.name: Total scheduled
dataFields.validation: The installments added together. Checked against the charge (BR-4).

dataFields.name: Decline reason
dataFields.validation: Maximum 500 characters. Required when declining a request (BR-3).
dataFields.example: A plan was agreed in March and two installments were missed.

dataFields.name: Reschedule reason
dataFields.validation: Maximum 500 characters. Required when changing an approved plan (BR-10).
dataFields.example: Family agreed a later second installment after the flood.
dataFields.requiredWhen: An approved plan is being rescheduled

businessRules.rule: A plan schedules a debt. It never changes how much is owed, only when it is paid.
The guardian states why they need a plan. It is what the School Admin weighs, and a request with no reason cannot be judged.
Accounts receive the request and define the schedule, but the School Admin approves it. A plan changes when the school is paid, so it is not one person's decision.
The installments must total exactly the outstanding charge. A plan that adds up to less is a discount granted by arithmetic, and a plan that adds up to more is a penalty nobody approved.
Each installment falls due later than the one before, and all fall within the academic session. A debt carried past the session it arose in is a different problem.
The original invoice is unchanged. The plan sits against it and the challan reflects the plan, but the charge itself is untouched.
While the plan is being met the student does not appear in overdue tracking, is not reminded, and accrues no late fee. This protection is the whole point of agreeing a plan.
A missed installment ends the protection at once. The student appears on the overdue list and late fee resumes, because a plan being broken is not a plan being kept.
A payment is applied to the earliest unpaid installment first. Otherwise a family paying an odd amount leaves the earliest part unmet while a later one is settled.
An approved plan may be rescheduled with a written reason, and the new schedule must still total the original charge. Rescheduling repeatedly is visible in the record.
A student holds one active plan per charge. A second request for the same charge is refused while one is running.
The plan is visible to whoever answers the counter, so a family paying as agreed is never told they are in arrears by somebody who did not know.
A guardian is told the decision either way. A request that disappears is worse than one that is declined.

transitions.condition: Approved, and Accounts define the schedule.
Declined with a written reason (BR-3, BR-13).
An installment is paid on or before its due date.
An installment passes its due date unpaid. The protection ends (BR-8).
The missed installment is paid, or the plan is rescheduled with a reason (BR-10).
The plan is abandoned. The full balance falls due at once.

alternateFlows.condition: The School Admin declines the request

alternateFlows.condition: The family asks at the office rather than through the app
alternateFlows.navigation: Login → Fee → Installment requests → Record request
alternateFlows.behaviour: Accounts record the request on the family's behalf with the reason they gave. Everything afterwards is identical.

alternateFlows.condition: An installment is paid late but before the next falls due
alternateFlows.navigation: Login → Fee → Payment plans → Record payment
alternateFlows.behaviour: The protection resumes once the missed installment is settled, and the plan returns to Active (BR-8).
The plan is rescheduled with a written reason. The new schedule must still total the original charge, and the rescheduling is visible in the record (BR-10).

alternateFlows.condition: A payment arrives that does not match an installment exactly
alternateFlows.behaviour: It is applied to the earliest unpaid installment first, so a family paying an odd amount does not leave the earliest part unmet (BR-9).
The plan is cancelled and the full outstanding balance falls due at once. The student returns to the ordinary overdue and late fee routes.

conventionsApplied.name: session-and-authentication
conventionsApplied.rule: Every use case except the login use case assumes an authenticated session. Sign out is available on every screen. An expired or invalid session returns the user to the login screen with the message "Your session has ended. Please sign in again."

conventionsApplied.name: role-based-access
conventionsApplied.rule: Access is enforced server-side on every request, not only by hiding menu items. A request for a record outside the actor's permitted scope returns a 403 and the message "You do not have permission to view this record." A use case states additions and restrictions only.

conventionsApplied.name: branch-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every record carries a branch ID. Users see only their own branch unless the use case states otherwise. Super Admin, School Admin and Principal may switch branch from the header.

conventionsApplied.name: academic-session-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every academic record carries an academic session ID. Lists default to the current open session.

conventionsApplied.name: list-screens
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list supports search, column sort and page-size selection. Default page size 25; default sort is most recent first. Filters are applied before printing or exporting.

conventionsApplied.name: print-and-pdf
conventionsApplied.rule: Every report and list offers Print and Download as PDF, honouring the filters currently applied. Each output carries the school name, branch, academic session, report title, filter summary, generation timestamp and the name of the user who generated it.

conventionsApplied.name: audit-trail
conventionsApplied.rule: Every create, update, deactivation, approval and reversal writes to the audit log: actor, role, timestamp, record type, record ID, before and after values, and IP address. Audit entries are never editable.

conventionsApplied.name: deletion
conventionsApplied.rule: Records are deactivated, not physically removed. Deactivated records are excluded from lists and lookups but remain in the audit trail and in historical reports. A record referenced by a financial transaction can never be deactivated.

conventionsApplied.name: validation-and-messages
conventionsApplied.rule: Field-level errors appear inline beneath the field on blur and on submit. Errors that block the whole action appear as a banner at the top of the form. Successful actions show a toast. No action succeeds silently.

conventionsApplied.name: money
conventionsApplied.rule: All monetary values are stored as fixed-point decimals in the smallest currency unit, never as floating point. Displayed as PKR with a thousands separator and two decimal places. Rounding is half-up at the line.

conventionsApplied.name: dates-times-numbers
conventionsApplied.rule: Dates display as DD-MM-YYYY; date and time as DD-MM-YYYY HH:mm in 24-hour form. Times are school-local. Phone numbers are stored in the registered mobile format.

conventionsApplied.name: language
conventionsApplied.rule: All user-visible strings come from a resource file. No hard-coded text in any screen.

conventionsApplied.name: concurrency-and-locking
conventionsApplied.rule: Last write wins, except where a use case defines an approval lock. Once a record is approved, posted or issued it becomes read-only and can only be changed through its defined reversal use case.

conventionsApplied.name: screen-states
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list, dashboard tile and report defines four states: loading, empty, error and populated. The empty state names what is missing and links to the action that creates it.

conventionsApplied.name: notifications
conventionsApplied.rule: All outbound SMS, WhatsApp, email and push messages are sent through the Messaging module, recorded in the sent-message log with per-channel delivery status, and use a named template. Use cases reference the template; they do not embed message text.

conventionsApplied.name: default-performance-and-retention
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise: a screen loads within 2 seconds and a save completes within 2 seconds at 200 concurrent users; lists paginate above 100 rows; financial and student records are retained 7 years; audit and message logs 12 months; every screen is usable at a 360 px viewport. Fill the non-functional field only to depart from this.

conventionsApplied.name: default-trigger
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise, the trigger is: the user navigates to the screen and initiates the action. Fill the Triggers field only where a scheduled job, an event in another module, or an inbound external call also starts it.
